body:
Burn-down complete (--status approved). Ready set drained to empty over 2 waves; no open PRs remain.

Completed:
  TASK-147 https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1553 - hook bodies sourced from master templates via include_str! (drift now structurally impossible)
  TASK-146 https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1554 - aida watch follow mode seeks to EOF instead of replaying history
  TASK-148 https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1555 - drain_lock borrow/force env isolated in acquire tests
  BUG-767  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1556 - awaiting mail_unread scoped to the operator's own inbox
  BUG-768  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1557 - rollup derivation no longer regresses force-closed epics
  BUG-769  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1558 - aida ps elapsed shows process uptime for an adopted lease
  BUG-770  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1559 - unit tests no longer write into the real .aida/events.jsonl

Caveats / verifications worth noting:
  - TASK-146's implementer disproved the spec's secondary hypothesis. The 162 duplicate STORY-306 advisor-escalated events were NOT a loop-appending escalation writer: finish_escalated resolves the project root from cwd, so every cargo test run has been appending synthetic escalations to the developer's real event log for months. That became BUG-770 and is now fixed. The already-written synthetic lines were deliberately left in place (real, if polluted, drain history) - a cleanup pass is an open call for you.
  - Wave 2 (BUG-769, BUG-770) was entirely self-generated: both were filed by wave-1 implementers mid-work. Worth noting the from-dogfood loop is producing real follow-ups faster than the gate drains them.
  - The integrated-main gate after each wave was a cargo build -p aida-cli compile check only, not a full test run. Each PR's own CI (Build ubuntu-latest) was green before merge, and every merge was polled to a terminal CI state - no PR was merged or abandoned while pending.
  - BUG-768's fix touches rollup derivation and cache; it shipped green but the epics it was meant to protect (EPIC-24, EPIC-0428) have not yet been re-observed across an overnight pull. Worth a look tomorrow to confirm they stay terminal.

Held / awaiting sign-off: none held as draft-only. 29 specs sit pickable-but-unqueued (awaiting_signoff) - up one during the drain from a newly filed spec. That set is yours to bless or reject; the drain never touched it.

Left for manual merge: none - all 7 PRs reached terminal CI, merged, and auto-bumped to Completed on pull.

Parked (with reason):
  TASK-735, TASK-751 - tagged deferred:on-demand
  TASK-749 - tagged deferred:future-rbac
  TASK-892 - tagged deferred:until-projects-toml-consumed
  EPIC-44 - epic, needs decomposition into bounded specs
  STORY-687, STORY-688 - tagged deferred:cockpit-phase2
  TASK-1004 - supervised, keyboard-only, never fanned out

Worktrees not pruned: none of mine - all 7 implementer worktrees and branches removed locally and on the remote. Three locked agent-* worktrees belong to other live sessions and were left alone. One stray branch, bug-768-rollup-force-closed-epics, points at a main ancestor with zero unique commits (not from this drain) - flagged, not deleted.
